title: Overdue Profiles and Occupancy Inspections: Occupancy and Residency Certification Desk Guidance
content:
## When an Occupancy and Residency Certification profile becomes overdue

A profile becomes overdue only when more than the response grace period — 30 calendar days under every plan — has passed since the cycle's due date without the cycle being complete. Those days are counted as calendar days starting the day after the certification due date, so the profile is still not overdue on the last grace day itself. The due date is read from the profile record.

| Day, counted from the due date (hypothetical due date on day 0) | Cycle incomplete | Overdue? |
|---|---|---|
| day 0 (the due date) to day 30 | yes | no — the last grace day, day 30, is still within the grace period |
| day 31 or later | yes | yes |
| any day | no (cycle complete) | no |

*Boundary case (hypothetical dates).* For a due date of 1 June, the thirtieth day after it is 1 July: on 1 July the profile is not yet overdue; on 2 July, with the cycle still incomplete, it is.

## Ordering an occupancy inspection

An occupancy inspection is ordered:

- within the plan's inspection-order window after a profile becomes overdue, with the reason **no certification response**;
- with the reason **returned mail**, when a certification request comes back undeliverable and the skip trace finds no new address within the plan's address-search period, as the plan's returned-mail setting provides;
- with the reason **vacancy report**, on a utility shut-off or vacancy report, as the plan's vacancy-report setting provides.

No more than the plan's per-cycle inspection limit is ordered in one cycle, counted as the inspections ordered on the profile whose certification year equals the calendar year of the profile's due date; a further trigger in the same cycle orders nothing. Each inspection carries the plan's occupancy inspection fee, which is added to the loan balance on the order date when the plan's fee-chargeable setting is yes.

## Recording the finding

An inspection result is recorded only against an inspection order on file for that profile that has no result yet. The vendor returns its finding within the plan's turnaround period, and the finding is always one of the plan's inspection findings.

| Finding | Effect |
|---|---|
| occupied by the borrower | does not complete the cycle, which still needs the required signatures |
| vacant | evidence for confirming non-occupancy |
| occupied by others | evidence for confirming non-occupancy |
| unable to determine | leads to a second inspection in the cycle when the plan's re-inspection setting is yes and the cycle limit allows |

*Hypothetical case.* An order already carrying a recorded finding cannot receive another; a second finding needs a second order on file.
